title: Petroleum, Natural Gas and Renewable Energy

cards.h: Energy security is a GS1 and GS3 favourite
cards.b: India imports about 85-88 percent of its crude oil and about half its natural gas. Domestic basins are small, so geography questions ask where oil and gas are found, and the shift to solar and wind is a recurring theme. Know the basins, the pipelines, and the renewable zones.

Oil is found in sedimentary basins where organic matter is trapped under cap rocks. India's basins:

  • Assam (Digboi, 1889, the oldest, Naharkatiya, Moran).
  • Gujarat (Ankleshwar, Kalol, Cambay basin).
  • Mumbai High (offshore, discovered 1974, the largest).
  • Krishna-Godavari (east coast).
  • Cauvery and Rajasthan (Barmer, Mangala field).

Found with oil or alone. Major fields: the KG basin (D6, Dhirubhai), Mumbai High, Tripura, Jaisalmer. Piped through the HBJ pipeline (Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur), 1,750 km, and the larger national grid. Uses: fertiliser, power, city gas, CNG. India's target is a 15 percent share of gas in the energy mix by 2030.

Refineries are at coastal and inland sites: Jamnagar (Reliance, the largest single-site refinery in the world), Vadinar, Mumbai, Kochi, Paradip, Mangalore, Digboi, Panipat, Mathura. Coastal sites suit imported crude. Inland refineries rely on pipelines. India depends heavily on West Asia, and since 2022 Russia has become the top supplier.

India stores crude in underground rock caverns: Visakhapatnam (1.33 million tonnes), Mangaluru (1.5) and Padur (2.5). They hold about 5.33 million tonnes, roughly 9-10 days of consumption. The Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (ISPRL) runs them. Phase II plans Chandikhol (Odisha) and Padur II.

India has about 300 sunny days in most regions. Solar parks: Bhadla (Rajasthan), among the world's largest, Pavagada (Karnataka), Kurnool, Charanka (Gujarat), Kamuthi (Tamil Nadu). The National Solar Mission (2010) was expanded. The International Solar Alliance (India and France, 2015) has its headquarters at Gurugram. The Modhera sun temple village in Gujarat became India's first 24-hour solar powered village.

Wind: Tamil Nadu leads, then Gujarat and Karnataka; offshore wind is being planned off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. Hydro: the Himalayan rivers, Western Ghats. Geothermal: Puga (Ladakh), Manikaran. Tidal: Gulf of Khambhat and Kachchh, Sundarbans. Biomass and waste-to-energy. Nuclear: Tarapur, Kudankulam, Kakrapar, Rawatbhata.

India aims for 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 (Panchamrit at COP26, 2021) and net zero by 2070. Instruments: PLI for solar modules, PM-KUSUM for farm solar, PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar (2024), National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023). Non-fossil capacity crossed 50 percent of installed capacity in 2025, as the government has announced.

Land use for solar parks, grid integration and storage, import dependence on Chinese solar cells, coal-state employment, and the cost of finance. A 'just transition' protects coal workers. Rajasthan's Great Indian Bustard habitat clashes with transmission lines, which went to the Supreme Court in 2021.

Likely questions: 'Why is India oil import dependent?', 'Potential of solar in India', 'Strategic petroleum reserves'.

  • Map: Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai High, KG basin.
  • Give numbers: import share and storage days.
  • Close with the policy mix: diversification, storage, renewables, green hydrogen.
